QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H fell from 0.520 on 2026-11-06 to 0.455 on 2026-11-13, below the independent finite-variance reference, 0.5. R²=0.936 measures fit only over scales 8–63. Short/long slopes, 0.393/0.648, mean one straight-line exponent fits poorly: possible crossover or transient volatility shift, not one clean scaling law.

H changed −0.024/−0.065 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-only 30-observation standardized deviation is −1.33; overlapping windows preclude a significance test. DFA-1 of magnitudes gives h_abs=0.759: stronger volatility-clustering persistence than near-0.5 signed returns, not tradable predictability.

Hill alpha rose from 3.198 on November 5 to 3.380, unchanged November 11–13. Its 1,000-return (~four-year) window uses k=100 and x_min=0.02018 absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha means heavier/thinner fitted tails, conditional on suitability. Idealized i.i.d. SE=alpha/√k=0.338 understates dependent-return uncertainty. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.593/3.039, not confidence bounds. Plateaus are normal when new returns miss top-k extremes, not static markets. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

interpretation.text:

Short-scale H=0.430 (8–20) versus long-scale 0.636 (25–63) means one straight-line exponent fits poorly: possibly crossover or transient volatility change, not one clean scaling law.

These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
